blocks.value: A program that cannot remember anything cannot do anything. Variables are how your program holds on to a score, a name, a price, a yes-or-no answer.

Java is strict about this in a way some languages are not: before you store a value, you must say exactly what *kind* of value it is. That feels like extra work at first. It is the reason the compiler can catch your mistakes before your users do.
What you will be able to do
By the end of this lesson you will be able to:

items: Name Java's eight primitive data types and choose the right one
Apply widening conversion and explicit casting
Predict what is lost when a value is narrowed
